fix_commit.message: avcodec/hevc/sei: prevent storing a potentially bogus num_ref_displays value in HEVCSEITDRDI
fix_commit.author: James Almer

findings.title: Truncation of num_ref_displays before range check leads to out-of-bounds array access
findings.message: In decode_nal_sei_3d_reference_displays_info(), the raw Exp-Golomb decoded value returned by get_ue_golomb(gb) (an unsigned int, which can be arbitrarily large, e.g. up to 2^32-1) is stored directly into s->num_ref_displays, a field declared as uint8_t in HEVCSEITDRDI. This assignment silently truncates the value modulo 256 BEFORE the bounds check 'if (s->num_ref_displays > 31)' is performed. As a result, an attacker-controlled bitstream value such as 287 (0x11F) truncates to 31 (0x1F), which passes the '> 31' check, and after the subsequent '+= 1' becomes 32. Because all of the per-display fixed-size arrays in HEVCSEITDRDI (left_view_id[31], right_view_id[31], exponent_ref_display_width[31], mantissa_ref_display_width[31], exponent_ref_viewing_distance[31], mantissa_ref_viewing_distance[31], additional_shift_present_flag[31], num_sample_shift[31]) are sized for at most 31 entries, the subsequent loop 'for (int i = 0; i < s->num_ref_displays; i++)' can write/read one or more elements past the end of these arrays, causing an out-of-bounds access (stack/heap buffer overflow) that was found by OSS-Fuzz.
findings.suggestion: Decode the Exp-Golomb value into a local unsigned variable (not the uint8_t struct field) and validate its range before ever narrowing/storing it into the uint8_t field, so the range check operates on the full, untruncated value.

ground_truth.root_cause: The unsigned value decoded from the bitstream via get_ue_golomb() was stored into a narrow uint8_t struct field before validating it, so the validation check operated on an already-truncated (wrapped) value instead of the original decoded value, defeating the intended upper-bound check of 31.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Truncation of num_ref_displays before range check leads to out-of-bounds array access
